'''Ōtori Shrine''' (大鷲神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Adachi, Tokyo|en|Adachi, Tokyo|qid=Q213464|lt=Adachi}}, Tokyo. It serves as the {{ill|Ubusunagami|en|Ubusunagami|qid=Q1392097|lt=Ubusunagami}} (guardian deity) of the Hanahata area and is also known as '''Hanahata Ōtori Shrine''' (花畑大鷲神社). It is considered the origin of the well-known {{ill|Tori-no-Ichi|ja|酉の市|1=Tori-no-Ichi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tori-no-Ichi|13=User:Immanuelle/Tori-no-Ichi|qq=}} markets, with its head shrine being {{ill|Ōtori taisha|en|Ōtori taisha|qid=Q705151|lt=Ōtori taisha}}. The shrine is featured in the {{ill|Edo meisho zue|en|Edo meisho zue|qid=Q2704637|lt=Edo meisho zue}}.{{sfn|Edo Meisho Zue|1927|p=521}}

== Overview ==

Surrounded by old and large trees, the shrine is situated in a serene environment teeming with various seasonal flora and fauna. Though typically tranquil, it attracts many visitors during {{ill|Hatsumōde|en|Hatsumōde|qid=Q1032381|lt=Hatsumōde}} (New Year’s visits) and {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|en|Shichi-Go-San|qid=Q1072387|lt=Shichi-Go-San}} celebrations in November. During the nights of {{ill|Tori-no-Ichi|ja|酉の市|1=Tori-no-Ichi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tori-no-Ichi|13=User:Immanuelle/Tori-no-Ichi|qq=}}, fireworks are displayed.

The shrine also preserves records of mathematical tablets ({{ill|Sangaku|en|Sangaku|qid=Q2569069|lt=Sangaku}}) dedicated by local Edo-period mathematicians. Among these, the "Hanahata Ōtori Shrine Sangaku," donated by Kanesugi Kiyotoki’s disciples in 1833, is registered as a tangible cultural property of Adachi Ward.{{Cite web|url=https://www.city.adachi.tokyo.jp/bunka/chiikibunka/bunkazai_ootorijinjasangaku.html|title=Hanahata Ōtori Shrine Sangaku|publisher=Adachi Ward|accessdate=2022-08-22}}

== History ==

=== Origins ===
The shrine's founding is attributed to the {{ill|Hōji (era)|en|Hōji (era)|qid=Q1327400|lt=Hōji}} period (1247–1249).{{sfn|Adachi Historical Society|1978|p=231}} It is said that during the {{ill|Gosannen War|en|Gosannen War|qid=Q1187411|lt=Later Three-Year War}}, the Heian-period military commander {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshimitsu|en|Minamoto no Yoshimitsu|qid=Q3083118|lt=Minamoto no Yoshimitsu}} prayed for victory at this location after witnessing an eagle. This marked the shrine’s establishment.{{sfn|Adachi Historical Society|1992|p=162}}

Initially referred to as {{ill|Ōtori Daimyōjin|ja|鷲明神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōtori Daimyōjin|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the shrine was renamed Ōtori Shrine following the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu bunri}} during the Meiji era. 

* The shrine is mentioned in a {{ill|Munafuda|ja|棟札|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōda|qq=}} dated to the first year of {{ill|Kan'ei|en|Kan'ei|qid=Q1192913|lt=Kan’ei}} (1624), indicating its existence prior to this date.
* The oldest extant stone artifacts date back to the second year of {{ill|Manji (era)|en|Manji (era)|qid=Q1145295|lt=Manji}} (1659).
* During the {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|qid=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō}} period, the shrine’s affiliated temple was {{ill|Shogakuin|ja|正覚院|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shōkaku-in|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11545644}}.
* The current shrine structure dates back to the Ansei era, with contributions from the {{ill|Kubota Domain|en|Kubota Domain|qid=Q1067720|lt=Kubota Domain}}’s Satake family. Its wooden columns feature carvings attributed to a disciple of {{ill|Hidari Jingorō|en|Hidari Jingorō|qid=Q2668220|lt=Hidari Jingorō}}.

=== deity ===
While {{ill|Yamato Takeru|ja|日本武尊|lt=Prince Yamato Takeru|3=ヤマトタケル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Takeru|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ヤマトタケル|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q461258}} is listed as the shrine’s current deity, historical records suggest that {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshimitsu|en|Minamoto no Yoshimitsu|qid=Q3083118|lt=Minamoto no Yoshimitsu}} was likely its original object of worship. The shrine received significant patronage from the Satake family and other clans claiming descent from Yoshimitsu.

== Events ==

* '''Third Sunday of July''' ({{ill|Marine Day|en|Marine Day|qid=Q1355833|lt=Marine Day}}): {{ill|Hanahata Ōtori Shrine Lion Dance|ja|花畑大鷲神社獅子舞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hanahata Ōtori Shrine Lion Dance|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (designated an intangible cultural property of Adachi Ward). The shrine’s {{ill|Three-Lion Dance|ja|三匹獅子舞|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Three-Lion Dance|qq=}} is performed.{{sfn|Adachi Historical Society|1978|p=232}}
* {{ill|Tori-no-Ichi|ja|酉の市|1=Tori-no-Ichi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tori-no-Ichi|13=User:Immanuelle/Tori-no-Ichi|qq=}}

== Access ==
* A 27-minute walk from {{ill|Yatsuka Station|en|Yatsuka Station|qid=Q8050280|lt=Yatsuka Station}} on the {{ill|Tobu Isesaki Line|en|Tobu Isesaki Line|qid=Q906598|lt=Tōbu Isesaki Line}} ({{OSM route map|start=35.81411,139.80140|goal=35.80924,139.82021|name=Route}}).
